r7-loadbearing.title: Load-bearing question: is g3's retrieval genuinely layout-agnostic in implementation, and are all fixed findings verified independently
r7-loadbearing.imperative: Verify each of the prior BLOCK's three findings landed as claimed (not by trusting the implementer's account), verify the two additional self-found SS2 instances, then trace concretely what g3 would write against SS7/SS8's text to answer: does binding Option A require only an adapter swap at the named seam, or does it still require rewriting part of g3's retrieval? Sweep independently for any other single-layout assumption. Record pass/fail with a finding.
r7-loadbearing.finding: PRIOR FINDINGS: (1) SS7 self-contradiction -- GENUINELY FIXED. 'Never moved / same path' is now explicitly scoped to Option B ('Shown here under Option B... the file itself never moves'), with Option A's parallel field-update-plus-move stated inline, and a closing sentence names content-preservation as the only settled property. (2) Membership-predicate seam -- PARTIALLY FIXED. is_episode_in_ordinary_search(episode_id) is a real named seam (SS7 lines ~418-443) with two adapters (directory check / status check), and SS8 was rewritten so the per-id retirement filter routes through it instead of naming a grep directly. This genuinely makes the PER-ID CHECK additive. (3) SS2 filename/path claim -- GENUINELY FIXED, basename vs full-path distinguished. The two self-found SS2 instances (id-sequence scan, query-primitive glob) are also genuinely fixed with explicit Option A/B treatment. LOAD-BEARING QUESTION -- traced concretely what g3 would write: 'enumerate non-retired episodes' (SS8) needs BOTH a base enumeration (where do candidate episode ids/files come from) AND the per-id filter. The seam covers only the filter half. SS8's text ('a deterministic scan that... calls the is_episode_in_ordinary_search() seam') never specifies the base scan's own mechanics, and no glob/path pattern is shown for it anywhere in the document (confirmed by grep: 'scan' and 'glob' occurrences are limited to SS2's id-sequence-derivation case, never to the retrieval primitives). This is the SAME layout-dependence SS2 explicitly resolved for its own sibling case (Option B: one glob over episodes/; Option A: union of episodes/active/*.md and episodes/retired/*.md) but SS7/SS8 do not extend that treatment to retrieval. A literal, naive implementation (a flat glob feeding the seam) would silently return nothing once Option A binds -- a real code change to g3's own scan logic, not an adapter swap -- so 'g3's primitives... do not change' (SS7's closing claim) is not yet demonstrated for the whole primitive, only for the filter half. SECONDARY: no write-side seam is named for g2's writer's actual retire mechanics (file-move vs field-only) even though the original hunt-preemption question named 'the writer's retire op' explicitly; likely lower risk since Option A's write is a strict superset of Option B's (diff-always, optional move-add), but the document does not say so, leaving it to inference where SS2/SS7's read-side treatment was made explicit. TERTIARY (low): SS9 (cross-worktree) continues using bare 'episodes/<id>.md' notation (lines 498, 503) relying entirely on SS2's blanket disclaimer rather than a local pointer; not a new contradiction, just unreinforced. README.md re-confirmed clean (uses basename-only notation, no bare full-path claim). SS1/SS3/SS4/SS5/SS6 confirmed unchanged and still correct (no regression). VERDICT ON THIS CHECK: fail -- the central rework claim ('additive, not a rewrite... g3's primitives do not change') is not yet fully substantiated; recommend one more targeted paragraph in SS7/SS8 (mirroring SS2's existing Option A/B glob-union treatment) making the base-scan enumeration explicitly layout-agnostic before this gate closes.
